_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); athletic footwear and apparel signals

pit_profile.why: NIKE: 'NIKE is the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world', and 'Virtually all of our products are manufactured by independent contractors' (its own FY2021 10-K); the industry 'is highly competitive on a worldwide basis', 'including adidas, Anta, ASICS, Li Ning, lululemon athletica, Puma, Under Armour and V.F. Corporation, among others', and 'the relative popularity of various sports and fitness activities and changing design trends affect the demand for our products': a demand and fashion risk, not an obsolescence one

theme_watch.reason: Live: NIKE's own FY2021 10-K says 'In addition, the competitive nature of retail, including shifts in the ways in which consumers shop, and the continued proliferation of digital commerce, constitutes a risk factor implicating our NIKE Direct and wholesale operations.' At the same time it sells online itself: 'Digital commerce sales were $9.1 billion for fiscal 2021 compared to $5.5 billion for fiscal 2020'. The stock trades at 36.3x FY22E — a premium. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing the shift away from physical retail into NIKE's own sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: NIKE: 'NIKE is the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world', and 'Virtually all of our products are manufactured by independent contractors' (its own FY2021 10-K); the industry 'is highly competitive on a worldwide basis', 'including adidas, Anta, ASICS, Li Ning, lululemon athletica, Puma, Under Armour and V.F. Corporation, among others', and 'the relative popularity of various sports and fitness activities and changing design trends affect the demand for our products': a demand and fashion risk, not an obsolescence one. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 2.54x; +58% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.77; conservative 2yr -12%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -35.7%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21 ex-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +9.7%/yr (Q3 rev ex-FX + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY18 median

BULL.desc: EPS +12.8%/yr (FY12-FY21 ex-FY18 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +20.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21 ex-FY18); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NKE (retrospective, 2022-04-22) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.54x (76.8% downside to Bear $30 / +30.2% upside to Bull $168) | Adj composite 2.14 vs market 2.91: gap -0.77 [OVERVALUED] | +58% above the EPP floor $82 (23x FY22E $3.56) | Conservative 2-yr case: -11.6% total (-5.8%/yr) | At 36.3x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $171 sits above the BULL case; futures orders not reported for Q3 FY22, forward revenues +8% (Q3 FY22 revenue ex-currency); e-commerce is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
